text:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT: Dedicated pool "dedicated-pool-acme-enterprise" nearing GPU capacity exhaustion (94% GPUs allocated). Multiple downstream request timeouts detected. Link: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/2015009999 :rotating_light:

sarah_k: seeing a spike from acme - churned traffic pattern after their nightly batch started?

raj_patel: confirmed. Metrics: 1500 concurrent sessions, avg queue wait 1.8s -> 4.2s in last 6m. GPU allocation shows 28/30 GPUs in use on the pool. Some pods OOM-killed earlier.

alex_m: @raj_patel any indication this is their normal traffic (cron) or a runaway job?

raj_patel: looks like a scheduled retrain/prefetch job they started at 02:00 UTC. It spikes KV cache loads and causes long token latencies. Not typical steady traffic.

jordan_oncall: paging oncall. I'm taking lead for mitigation while oncall team escalates. Oncall runbook step 1: assess customer impact and whether to enable burst from shared capacity.

infra-bot: Current shared burst capacity: 8 GPUs available in region-us-west-2. Estimated cold-start time for burst nodes: ~90s. Auto-burst is disabled for this tenant (policy: enterprise-isolated).

sarah_k: customer impact: a portion of requests are failing with 504 after 15s. CS reported two support tickets: one production job stuck, one user-facing timeout. @eva_cs can you confirm severity and message to customer?

eva_cs: confirmed. Tickets show errors from 3 production apps. CS recommends offering immediate mitigation and a callback. I'll draft a short status update once we decide mitigation.

raj_patel: mitigation options: 1) temporarily override isolation and permit burst from shared pool (needs infra approval), 2) throttle ACME tenant at routing layer to protect pool, 3) trigger failover to a cheaper/more compact model variant for non-critical routes, 4) ask ACME to pause scheduled job.

alex_m: preference is combination: throttle non-critical endpoints + request burst for emergency window. That avoids full isolation override long-term. How do we throttle quickly?

jordan_oncall: we can flip a routing rule to reduce per-tenant concurrency and limit tokens per request. Command: `curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/tenants/acme/actions -d '{"action":"set_limit","concurrency":50,"max_tokens":512}'` (ops key required).

raj_patel: I'll prepare the route change. Also running `kubectl describe pods -n pools dedicated-pool-acme-enterprise` now to check pod restarts.

infra-bot: Pod report: 3 restarts in last 10m on model-worker-7, kernel memory pressure observed; quantized model variant fallback available on the same pool (smaller memory).

raj_patel: route change applied. Reduced concurrency to 50 and set max_tokens 512 for tenant acme. Observed queue depth drop from 1500 -> 900 in ~2m. Latency improving for critical routes.

jordan_oncall: next, request burst approval. @sarah_k do you have authority to enable temporary burst override for incidents?

sarah_k: I can approve emergency override for up to 30 minutes. File a change with reason and remediation plan.

alex_m: I'll file change: `INC-2015009999 - emergency burst for dedicated-pool-acme-enterprise, enable 6 GPUs from shared pool, 30m window, rollback at 30m or when queue < 200`

infra-bot: Burst request accepted. Provisioning 6 GPUs from shared pool. Estimated join 75s.

raj_patel: provisioning happening. Starting to route low-priority traffic to quantized variant to reduce memory pressure.

jordan_oncall: monitoring: queue depth trending down to 420, 95th latency down from 6.2s -> 2.3s. Error rate decreased from 4.1% -> 1.2%. Good.

eva_cs: I sent ACME a short message: "We are investigating elevated latency on your dedicated pool and have applied temporary traffic limits while we add emergency capacity. We'll follow up in 15m with an update."

sarah_k: good. Keep CS message concise and honest. We should avoid saying "burst override" in customer message; say "additional capacity".

raj_patel: 6 GPUs joined. Pool now at 34/36 logical GPUs. Load per GPU reduced. No further OOMs seen in last 3m.

alex_m: plan for the next hour: 1) keep throttle rules, 2) monitor for queue <200 to rollback throttle, 3) keep burst for 30m then auto-return to isolation, 4) open follow-up task to discuss tenant scheduled workloads and autoscaling policy for enterprise pools.

jordan_oncall: agree. Assign follow-up: ENG-INFRA ticket to evaluate autoscale thresholds + tenant-scheduled-job detection. I'll create ticket and assign to raj + alex.

raj_patel: creating ticket ENG-INFRA-2015: investigate autoscale policy for dedicated pools, consider safe emergency-burst exceptions, and recommended SLOs.

infra-bot: Burst window set to expire at 2015011740 (30m). Auto-rollback scheduled.

jordan_oncall: handing off to day oncall @alex_m in 10m. I'll keep monitoring for 15m then sign off. If anything spikes, page me.

alex_m: taking handoff. Thanks @jordan_oncall. I'll monitor the next 40m and coordinate postmortem.

sarah_k: good work. After we stabilize, CS to propose a runbook change for enterprise customers to disable heavy scheduled jobs or provide a 'batch' flag that routes jobs to a non-production pool.

eva_cs: noted. I'll draft suggested customer guidance and loop in AM.

raj_patel: last check: queue at 180, errors ~0.6%, latency stable. Dropping non-critical routes to quantized model helped.

infra-bot: Burst GPUs will be returned at 2015011740 unless extended by an authorized approver.

jordan_oncall: closing active mitigation. Leaving this thread for postmortem notes. Will create postmortem doc after 24h with timeline and RCA.

alex_m: logged immediate RCA notes. Postmortem owner: alex_m. I'll link to doc once created. :memo:

sarah_k: thanks all. Great cross-team coordination. :thumbsup:
